verification_scope: Checkpoint hashes, all 218 IDs and metric CSV means verified for completed runs. Independently recomputed nine scores/counts for all 12 saved second-seed best/final arrays, all differences exactly 0. No full 218-image re-inference.
plot_observations: Both L400 seeds reach their best early (200 and 500 attempted updates), then show validation rebound while online training loss continues falling. Second seed rebounds less in absolute AbsRel, but neither has a terminal 500-step interval within 1% of its own best.
Both confirm the <=0.10 target at step 300. Second seed has a best <0.09, yet no three-consecutive-evaluation <=0.09 window; the stricter target panel correctly remains unattained.

Available-seed sample-efficiency plots show L400 lower overall error but lower best F1 than L200, and higher F1 than R400. These plotted means use 2 L400 versus 3 older completed seeds, so conclusions below rely on the separately matched two-seed statistics.

Stopping F1 has a large dip for L200 driven by its first-seed endpoint collapse. The apparent L400 rebound is not evidence of a consistent improvement across seeds: final F1 improves by 0.1410 for the first pair but declines by 0.00868 for the second.

The stable-at-end panel has no L400 point; missing convergence is not zero iterations. R400 has two of three stable runs, whereas available L400 runs reach better validation minima and stop earlier without satisfying this stability definition.
conclusions: L400 best AbsRel is 0.0897604 +/- 0.0004157 across two seeds; F1 is 0.4638504 +/- 0.0016222. These are interim two-seed statistics, not the requested final three-seed result.

Versus matched L200, both seeds improve best AbsRel, mean difference -0.00295066. The scene-bootstrap upper endpoint is -2.62e-7, effectively at zero; this boundary result is not presented as robust statistical evidence. Other best-metric intervals cross zero, including F1 despite both seed means declining.

Versus matched R400, both seeds improve best AbsRel and best F1. Mean differences -0.00560942 and +0.01345567 have conditional scene intervals excluding zero. RMSE, delta1 and boundary-band intervals cross zero.
Versus B0, all five best metrics improve in both available seeds and their conditional scene intervals exclude zero. Existing difficult-scene failures remain documented in the first-seed review.

Endpoint AbsRel worsens by 2.68% and 2.27% relative to the respective validation minima. Endpoint F1 moves in opposite directions, +0.006518 and -0.009153; its paired average interval crosses zero. Boundary-band error improves by about 0.00269 in both. Preserve best/final rather than selecting a new checkpoint by edge scores.

Second-seed predicted edge pixels decline from 484659 at best to 448210 at final; matched GT edges from 308175 to 294133 with the same 769528 GT edge pixels. This supports the recorded recall decrease; it does not establish a mechanism or onset during training.

LoRA allocated peak memory remains 4019.69 MiB; total elapsed times 759.33 and 953.86 s include validation and detailed scoring. Second seed records one AMP skip, 1499 successful updates of 1500 attempted; no configuration changes or retry.

Third L400 seed is still required. Continue unchanged to J400 and all later planned data sizes/methods. The 200-to-400 comparison is interim; 300 will be included before final adjacent-count analysis.
limitations: Conditional scene bootstrap with 2000 replicates and seed 320119; two training seeds provide weak variability characterization. No multiplicity adjustment, no blind test claim, no new test evaluation. Early stopping endpoint comparisons share validation-based checkpoint selection and are descriptive.
